title: Comparison of fibre products over different algebraic-space bases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $A,B,Z,T$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A\to Z$, $B\to Z$ and $h:Z\to T$ be morphisms. Form sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the canonical comparison $i:A\times_ZB\to A\times_TB$ with the two original projections as components. Then $i$ is representable by schemes, a monomorphism (injective on sections over every $S$-scheme), locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated, and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For the two local properties, this means that after every scheme base change to its target the resulting scheme morphism has the stated property. Separated means that the relative diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $h$ is quasi-separated, meaning that its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests, then $i$ is quasi-compact: after every affine scheme base change its source is quasi-compact (every open covering has a finite subcover).

proof.text: Write $f:A\to Z$, $g:B\to Z$, $P=A\times_ZB$, $Q=A\times_TB$ and $W=Z\times_TZ$. These are algebraic spaces with the indicated sheaf universal properties by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Define $q:Q\to W$ by $(a,b)\mapsto(f(a),g(b))$. It lands in $W$ because $hf(a)=hg(b)$ on $Q$. The map $i$ forgets the stronger equality $f(a)=g(b)$ and keeps the same pair. Consequently it is injective on sections over every $S$-scheme. There is a natural isomorphism $P\cong Q\times_{W,\Delta_h}Z$: its forward map sends $(a,b)$ to $((a,b),f(a))$, and its inverse forgets $z$ in a triple $((a,b),z)$ with $f(a)=z=g(b)$. The two formulas are inverse and commute with restrictions, and the projection to $Q$ is $i$.

source.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), displayed cartesian square, expanded on sections.

proof.text: Let $C$ be any $S$-scheme and $c:h_C\to Q$ any map. Composing with $q$ gives a scheme test $qc:h_C\to W$ of $\Delta_h$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests] with its base $B=S$, its morphism $g=h:Z\to T$, and its test scheme equal to $C$. It gives a scheme $D_C=Z\times_Wh_C$ whose projection $d_C:D_C\to C$ is locally of finite type and a monomorphism. The isomorphism of step 1 identifies $P\times_Qh_C$ with $D_C$ over $C$: a section is a map $u:H\to C$ together with the forced value $z=f(a(u))=g(b(u))$. Thus every scheme test of $i$ is represented by this scheme and has the asserted local finite type property. This is representability in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03KN, base change of the relative diagonal; Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), scheme-test formulation of (1)--(3).

proof.text: For each test in step 2, apply [lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf] to the scheme morphism $d_C:D_C\to C$ followed by $\mathrm{id}_C$. The composite is $d_C$, which is locally of finite type, and $d_C$ is a monomorphism; both hypotheses were supplied by [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests]. The cited conclusion gives local quasi-finiteness in the affine-neighbourhood sense, and hence in the required scheme-morphism sense, for every such test. No quasi-compactness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 03HK proof, last paragraph, local quasi-finiteness of a locally finite type monomorphism; scheme inputs Tags 02GE and 02V5.

proof.text: Put $R=P\times_QP$, with projections $r_1,r_2$. From $ir_1=ir_2$ and the sectionwise injectivity in step 1 we have $r_1=r_2$. The diagonal $\delta:P\to R$ satisfies $r_1\delta=1_P$, and both projections of $\delta r_1$ equal those of $1_R$; the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] therefore gives $\delta r_1=1_R$. Thus $\Delta_i$ is an isomorphism. Every scheme test of it is represented by its test scheme with the identity projection. The identity is a homeomorphism onto the whole closed subset and induces an isomorphism, hence a surjection, on structure sheaves. It is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves separatedness in exactly the stated sense.

source.place: Tag 03KN, monomorphism and separatedness; Tag 03HK proof, last sentence (scheme diagonal-isomorphism argument expanded for sheaves).

proof.text: Finally assume $h$ is quasi-separated as defined in the statement. For an affine scheme $C$ and $c:h_C\to Q$, the composite $qc:h_C\to W$ is an affine scheme test of $\Delta_h$. Its pullback $Z\times_Wh_C$ is quasi-compact by that hypothesis. By the explicit identification in step 2 it is the same scheme as the pullback $P\times_Qh_C$ of $i$. Hence the source of every affine scheme test of $i$ is quasi-compact, exactly the required assertion. This uses the hypothesis only in this final step and no finiteness hypothesis on $A$, $B$, $Z$, $T$ or $S$.

source.place: Tag 03KN (4), using the displayed cartesian square and the definition of quasi-separatedness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), cartesian-diagonal proof; Tag 03HK proof, final paragraph. Sectionwise identifications and the monomorphism diagonal argument are written out.

The item states exactly 03KN clauses (1) and (4), with their meanings spelled out, so nothing is weakened. It is the first delivery, and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live. There are no new nodes and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 1 is elementary and correct: on sections P is inside Q, so i is injective, and P is isomorphic to Q x_{W,Delta_h} Z. Step 2 applies the statement of lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests (U=Z, V=T, test C via qc): D_C is a scheme and d_C is locally of finite type and a monomorphism. Through step 1, D_C is P x_Q h_C, which gives representability as defined in def-trf-algebraic-space. Step 3 applies lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf with g = id; both hypotheses come from step 2, and the conclusion is local quasi-finiteness in the pqf (2) sense. Step 4 is elementary: since i is injective, the diagonal of i is an isomorphism, so every scheme test of it is an identity, which is a closed immersion. Step 5 is elementary: an affine test of i is an affine test of Delta_h, so its source is quasi-compact under either reading of the hypothesis. I checked the edge cases: h = id gives an isomorphism; for the line with doubled origin, i is the diagonal, an immersion that is not closed, which is consistent because clause (3) is not claimed; a non-quasi-compact diagonal gives no conclusion; empty and nonreduced tests cause no problem. Searching the DAG for 03KN found no duplicate, and the cited closures contain no cycle. Batch 5: def-trf-algebraic-space (reached through the diagonal-tests node) is a general definition and lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf is a generic scheme lemma (Stacks 01L4, 02GE, 02V5); neither closure reaches a trace-formula or Poincare node, so both are accepted. lean.statement: theorem fibreProduct_comparison_properties {S : Scheme.{u}} (A B Z T : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : A ⟶ Z) (g : B ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ T) : IsRepresentable (pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom ∧ (∀ C : Over S, Function.Injective ((pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom.app (op C))) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ LocallyOfFiniteType p.left) (pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal (pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite p.left) (pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom ∧ (IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) (pullback.diagonal h.hom.hom) → IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) (pullback.mapDesc f.hom g.hom h.hom).hom)
